messages:
Ravi K.: Heads-up: DSAR inbound from EU user wants full erasure of chat history and derived vectors, plus an auditable proof packet. Req#: EU-2026-214.

Nora V.: Is this hosted or dedicated? key ownership matters.

Ravi K.: Hosted. user_id: usr_21b. No cross-tenant pointers but they mention an old exported transcript.

kms-bot: Affected keys: embeddings-store -> platform-key-v4, snapshot-archive -> snapshot-key-2023-Q4.

Leo M.: Practical constraints: backups + cold archives may hold copies. We need to map retention windows and whether archives are encrypted under platform keys or archive-only keys.

Priya (Legal): We need: (1) manifest of deleted objects, (2) raw audit-line export showing delete operations with operator principal, (3) operator-signed statement. No key rotations without explicit legal sign-off.

Nora V.: Proposed safe flow:
- Create ephemeral RBAC role `dsar_exec_usr21b` scoped to user_id=usr_21b, TTL 6h.
- Dry-run to enumerate objects (convos, embeddings, index refs, snapshots). Produce manifest dryrun.json.
- Canary: delete single embedding shard and confirm no rebuilds.
- Pause relevant backup & snapshot jobs.
- Run full deletion in order: derived artifacts -> indexes -> raw objects -> snapshots.
- Run tombstone compaction and replication-consistency checks.
- Export audit-lines and attach signed manifest.

Leo M.: Replication note: eu-west replicas have delayed async apply. After deletion we must verify none of the replicas will be used for point-in-time restores. I'll run a replica sweep and flag any recent restores.

Ravi K.: Also check whether embeddings were materialized into any searchable cache (Redis caches). Those caches are TTLed but may persist. Must purge caches.

audit-bot: Reminder: audit pipeline retains raw logs for 90 days by default. Legal asked for 180 days for DSAR evidence. Please request retention-exception if needed.

Priya (Legal): Confirmed: request retention-exception for 180 days for DSAR EU-2026-214. We will countersign the final package. Operator signature must include name and role plus the standard attestation line.

Nora V.: Draft manifest schema (will be signed):
[ {object_path: "gs://prod/users/usr_21b/chat-2026-03-01.json", object_id: "chat-2026-03-01", storage: "object-store", kms_key: "snapshot-key-2023-Q4", derived: ["emb-2026-03-01"], deletion_ts: "2026-06-11T11:22:00Z", method: "api-delete", operator: "Nora V.", proof_hash: "sha256:..."} ]

Priya (Legal): Add fields `request_id` and `scope` (hosted/dedicated). Include operator role string. Fine to use SHA256 hash and PGP sign.

Leo M.: Technical caveat: embeddings DB uses soft deletes -> tombstones. We'll run compaction immediately after deletion and verify `SELECT count(*) FROM vectors WHERE user_id='usr_21b'` returns 0. Also purge search-cache keys: `redis-cli KEYS usr_21b*` then delete.

Ravi K.: Who's owning the ephemeral RBAC? Nora?

Nora V.: I'll open the RBAC PR and create the dry-run manifest in gs://compliance/dsar/EU-2026-214/dryrun.json. PR will include TTL 6h and a JIT approval list.

OpsTeam: Created ticket DSAR-214. Backup pause scheduled pending canary success.

Ravi K.: Can we avoid destructive KMS ops? prefer traceable deletes over key rotation.

Priya (Legal): Absolutely. Only legal-approved key destruction allowed. We'll prefer manifest+signed audit outputs.

Nora V.: Canary scheduled in 30m. Will post results. If canary passes we'll pause backups and run full erase today.

Leo M.: I'll prepare replica sweep scripts and tombstone compaction runbook.

audit-bot: Retention-exception request created: RET-214 (180 days).

Priya (Legal): Once ops uploads signed manifest I'll countersign and prepare response to requester.

Ravi K.: Recap: Nora -> RBAC + dry-run + canary. Leo -> replica & compaction checks. Ops -> pause backups + export audits. Priya -> legal sign-off and retention-exception.

Nora V.: PR: https://git.redwood/infra/rbacs/PR-214. Dry-run path: gs://compliance/dsar/EU-2026-214/dryrun.json.

Ravi K.: Thanks. Keep this thread for canary status updates only.
